script: I thought I could post, but moderators ruined my plan.. I just hit the "post" button and the whole subreddit lit up with the new rule: you got to be a legit account, have some karma, or you're out of here. (Micro‑hook: "The new rule hit harder than a surprise pop‑up ad.") I am not the only one who cares about the fine print; the mods are like, "If you're a throwaway, slide us a modmail from your main account with a link to the post you want to get approved." They promise to keep your info under lock‑down, but they're straight‑up firm—no wiggle room. So I sat there, fingers hovering over the keyboard, thinking about how this is basically a gatekeeper for the internet's hottest gossip. Imagine you're scrolling for that juicy tea, and suddenly the screen pops with a "You're not allowed" message because your account is still fresh. The stakes? My whole vibe of staying in the loop. I couldn't even comment on the latest celeb drama. The weight was real—like, my scroll life felt blocked. I tried to reason with myself: "It's just rules." But then I remembered how many times I've seen people get locked out because they didn't meet the threshold. The audacity of that policy felt like a personal smack. I am not just saying this for a few; this is the new reality for every bestie who wants to drop a comment. The tension builds: I hit "send" on the modmail, hoping the approval comes through. Minutes feel like hours. Then I get a ping—"Approved." The relief? It's like finding a secret password to a hidden club. The moment you're in, the vibe changes. The rest of the post feels like it's breathing easier. I am still better than the people who can't get in—because I know the hustle, I know the grind. And honestly, that's the tea. The end? I am back in the conversation, scrolling, laughing, and letting the rest of the world know that the new rules didn't stop me.
